summary: The functional optimization is correct — the first added AlterModelManagers branch correctly reduces CreateModel + AlterModelManagers to a single CreateModel. However, the same identical elif block is inserted FIVE times, and four of those copies are unreachable dead code, which a Django maintainer would refuse to merge.

issues.description: The exact same `elif isinstance(operation, AlterModelManagers) and self.name_lower == operation.name_lower` block is added 5 times at different positions in the if/elif chain (52 of the 65 added lines). In a Python if/elif chain only the first matching branch runs; since all five conditions are byte-for-byte identical, only the first one (after the DeleteModel branch) ever executes. Blocks 2–5 are dead, unreachable code. The correct fix is a single branch.

Four duplicated/unreachable copies of the same reduction logic severely harm readability and maintainability — future readers must reason about why the block repeats, and any later edit risks updating only some copies. This is not a minor nit; it is a structural defect that must be collapsed to one branch.

Scattering the new branch across multiple insertion points (rather than placing one branch in the chain) suggests a copy-paste implementation that doesn't reflect how the if/elif dispatch actually works; the approach is fragile and inconsistent with the single-branch pattern used by the adjacent AlterModelOptions reduction.
